chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fazala ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar or Ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: For every salat there are two times — the beginning of the time is the better of the two.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُهُمَا: The more meritorious / better of the two — indicates that the early time carries greater spiritual reward
key_terms.صَلَاة: Salat — the obligatory ritual prayer; one of the Five Pillars of Islam
key_terms.وَقْتَانِ: Two prayer-times — refers to the primary (fadhila) and secondary (ijza') time windows for each obligatory prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it better to pray salat at the beginning of its time in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that each prescribed prayer has two valid time windows: an early window (the preferred time, from the call to prayer until roughly midpoint) and a late window (still valid but less meritorious). Performing salat at the earliest permissible moment is considered more virtuous. This ruling reflects the Imami jurisprudential view that prompt fulfillment of religious obligations demonstrates greater devotion.
word_analysis: is the better of the two
